recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future DAF, QICore, or Extension Pack content problems should be handled in those IGs or their current repositories unless a specific current core page becomes misleading.
issue_request: FHIR-7759 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core DSTU1 clarification asking that implementers be able to tell where core extensions ended and DAF or QICore extensions began, with an area for each defining body to describe extensions and make them accessible from profile publication.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-7759. The issue appears to have been applied through the 2015 publishing reorganization: DAF and other IG artifacts were moved into guide directories, IG links were moved to subdirectories, and profile/extension registry pages began listing implementation guides that define profiles and extensions.
additional_context: The current source distinguishes the base FHIR platform and its base extensions from implementation guides that define additional profiles and extensions for particular contexts. Extensibility rules point implementers to the FHIR Extension Pack, implementation guides, registries, and publisher/contact metadata. The active core build configuration no longer owns old DAF or QICore profile/extension definitions.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Adding extra prose to the current core profiling page would duplicate existing guidance and could imply that old DAF/QICore material should be re-owned by core, contrary to the publishing-paradigm resolution and current IG/Extension Pack split.

related_jiras.note: A later Published QICore-specific issue about authoring QICore extensions as separate entities; it supports that QICore extension organization belongs to the QICore IG track rather than this core audit.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive DSTU1 clarification asking where core, DAF, and QICore extensions begin and end.
evidence_items.learned: The accepted resolution was to sort this out through the new IG publishing paradigm, not by adding a new current conformance rule.

evidence_items.summary: The profiling page separates the base FHIR platform and base extensions from profiles and implementation guides governed by different communities.
evidence_items.learned: Current core narrative already provides the core-versus-IG boundary requested by FHIR-7759.

evidence_items.summary: The extensibility page directs implementers to the FHIR Extension Pack, implementation guides, registries, and publisher/contact metadata for extension definitions.
evidence_items.learned: Current extensibility rules cover extension discoverability and ownership without needing FHIR-7759-specific prose.

evidence_items.summary: The active core profile/extension configuration omits DAF and QICore definitions; current site links separate FHIR Extensions and Implementation Guides, with old DAF/QICore IG entries commented out in source/igs.xml.
evidence_items.learned: The current build organization reflects the IG publishing split and does not require a core source edit for old DAF/QICore extension ownership.

evidence_items.summary: 2015 history moved DAF/USLab content into guide directories, moved IG links to subdirectories, and added implementation-guide registry listings for profiles and extensions.
evidence_items.learned: FHIR-7759 was effectively applied as part of historical publishing infrastructure work rather than a single Jira-tagged patch.
